messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: auth-proxy anomalous pattern detected. Sudden replay-like traffic using previously-seen tokens from 3 external IPs. Potential leaked/debug log tokens. Paging @alex (oncall). Severity: P2. Link: https://pager/incidents/3141592700
alex: Acked, I'm on it — putting a triage channel together. Who has the latest auth logs?
maria: I’m pulling logs now, running a token frequency scan across proxy-logs. Will post findings in a sec.
maria: quick grep I ran: `grep -E "token_id=[a-z0-9]+" /var/log/proxy/* | awk -F"token_id=" '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head`
maria: snippet from proxy logs (redacted):
```
2024-08-01T13:45:02 proxy INFO req_id=R1 src=3.23.45.67 token_id=tok_abc123 status=200 user=tenant-42
2024-08-01T13:45:03 proxy INFO req_id=R2 src=3.23.45.67 token_id=tok_abc123 status=200 user=tenant-42
2024-08-01T13:45:06 proxy INFO req_id=R3 src=18.204.11.9 token_id=tok_x9z status=200 user=tenant-77
```
maria: Observations: same token used repeatedly from single IPs, and two different tenants show token reuse. Not system-wide auth failures, but successful accesses using leaked tokens.
linda: Confirming infra side — I just checked the staging uploader config and an S3 job had `include: /var/log/debug/*.log` in its manifest. It's been pushing to bucket `redwood-debug-archive-2024`. Running `aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-debug-archive-2024` now.
linda: ACL output: `Grantee: AllUsers, Permission: READ` — bucket is publicly readable. :grimacing:
emily: Yikes. That bucket was intended to be private for internal debugging only. I can disable the uploader and flip ACLs now.
alex: Immediate actions: 1) block suspicious IPs at WAF (linda), 2) disable the staging uploader and set bucket to private (emily), 3) rotate any tokens that we confirm were exposed (maria), 4) preserve evidence snapshot for legal (jonathan). Who can own each?
linda: I’ll push WAF block rule for the three IPs: 3.23.45.67, 18.204.11.9, 52.11.22.33. Applying and rate-limiting now.
emily: disabling uploader and setting ACL to private now — `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-debug-archive-2024 --acl private` — done. Also creating a snapshot copy to internal-only bucket before we remove objects.
maria: For token rotation: recommend force-rotating service tokens for tenant-42 and tenant-77 and invalidating any active sessions tied to exposed token ids. Runbook snippet: `runbook/auth/rotate-service-token --tenant tenant-42 --force` then `auth-api invalidate-session --token tok_abc123`. I can execute if ops approves.
jonathan: Legal here — capture a full listing of objects and their ACLs and lock evidence. Also list any PII patterns in logs (emails, user ids). I'll need a preserved copy.
sam: Customer Success / comms — I'll draft an initial holding message for affected customers once we confirm tenant list. Sam: I can also start the internal incident report template.
alex: Execute rotation for tenant-42 and tenant-77 now. Maria and Emily, coordinate on session invalidation and token rotate. Linda, keep WAF block in place for 2 hours then reassess. Jonathan, snapshot evidence and flag any PII. Sam, prep CS draft but hold sending until we confirm impacted tenants and a mitigation ETA.
maria: Running rotation commands:
```
# rotate tokens + invalidate
rotate-service-token --tenant tenant-42 --mode force && auth-api invalidate-session --tenant tenant-42 --pattern "tok_*"
rotate-service-token --tenant tenant-77 --mode force && auth-api invalidate-session --tenant tenant-77 --pattern "tok_*"
```
maria: Rotations kicked off — services will gracefully fail-over to new tokens. Monitoring for auth errors.
linda: WAF blocks in place. Confirmed 0 new requests from blocked IPs in the last 30s.
emily: Bucket ACL set to private and objects copied to `redwood-evidence/quarantine/3141592700`. Preserved versioning enabled.
jonathan: Evidence snapshot done. I’ve locked the quarantine bucket with restricted access and filed a legal hold. Noted potential PII; will follow up via secure channel.
sam: Drafted CS note (internal): "We detected tokens possibly exposed via an internal debug archive. We have rotated affected tokens and isolated the storage. We are investigating scope and will update within 2 hours." Will refine after legal confirms wording.
alex: Quick customer-impact summary for incident channel: tenants confirmed impacted: tenant-42, tenant-77. No broad outage; access was possible for those token values until invalidation. No confirmed exfil of user content beyond what’s in debug logs (still under review).
emaria: Monitoring auth metrics — slight spike in 401->200 conversions while tokens live, now trending down after invalidation. Will run a prompt scan to find any other token IDs referenced in S3 objects: `grep -E "token_id=[a-z0-9]+" /mnt/quarantine/* | sort | uniq`.
emaria: Found ~6 token ids across debug files; rotated associated tenants where applicable.
jonathan: Legal: moving to high priority — prepare to include affected customers in a secure notification if PII exposure confirmed.
alex: Ownership: I’ll run initial post-incident review draft. Sam will take lead on customer comms after legal signoff. Maria/linda/emily keep monitoring for 24h. Jonathon, legal on evidence and escalation. If anything new pops, re-alert pager.
sam: Taking next shift handoff in 30m — I'll watch the channel and pick up updates.
alex: Thanks everyone — marking triage complete and moving to monitoring+postmortem workstream. Closing active mitigation at 2024-08-01T14:01:05. :white_check_mark:
